name: אֲחִיעֶזֶר
summary: Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was the prince of Dan in the wilderness: he stood with Moses at the numbering, brought Dan’s offering on the tenth day of the altar’s dedication, and led Dan’s standard as the rear guard of all the camps (Num 10:25). A second Ahiezer led the Benjamite archers who came to David at Ziklag (1Ch 12:3). The name is אֲחִי “brother of, my brother” with עֵזֶר “help”: “my brother is help”, the same build as אֱלִיעֶזֶר, “my God is help”, which Moses explains as “the God of my father was my help” (Exo 18:4). The “brother” is most likely God, as in other names in אֲחִי־.

evidence.note: Prince of the sons of Dan, on the north side of the camp.
His offering on the tenth day; 7:71 “this was the offering of Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai”.
The standard of the camp of Dan set out last, “gathering up all the camps”, and over its host אֲחִיעֶזֶר בֶּן־עַמִּישַׁדָּי.
“The chief was אֲחִיעֶזֶר, then Joash, the sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite”, among the Benjamites who came to help David (12:1).
The same pattern in אֱלִיעֶזֶר, explained by the text: “the God of my father was בְּעֶזְרִי”.

note: Root key עזר for the element עֶזֶר; the first element אֲחִי is the root אחה (entry ach). Ammishaddai (עַמִּישַׁדָּי), his father, has no name entry yet. The reading of “brother” as God rests on the pattern of names in אֲחִי־ and אֱלִי־ (Ahijah, “my brother is Yah”), not on a verse that says so; review. Phoenician names of the type ʿzrbʿl and Ugaritic yʿḏr-addu are the cognate name-type (see the cognates in ezer.json).
